thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered for REDWOOD-API - SLO burn-rate alert (rule: SLOBurnHigh) at 1718001234
Jordan: seeing a spike in p99 latency + elevated error rate for text-generation. getting a flood of `429` and backend GPU timeouts. paging because burn-rate > 10 for 5m window.
Maria: I'm on it. preliminary customer-impact: ~3% of requests failing, mostly hosted customers hitting larger batch sizes.
Kevin: @Jordan how many active Dedicated clusters affected? might be routing issue.
Jordan: Dedicated looks fine. it's the hosted inference pool in us-east-1. routing fallback kicked in but slow.
Samira: logs show OOMs in runtime on model-variant xlarge-q4, kv-cache spikes. attaching snippet:```
2026-04-10T12:07:21Z runtime ERROR kvcache: reserve failed: out of memory
2026-04-10T12:07:23Z worker WARN request dropped: batch queue full
```
Avery: adding ops runbook link: https://confluence/internal/runbooks/slo-burn
Maria: live mitigation: lowering concurrency on the autoscaler for hosted pool to reduce batch compaction. rolling throttle on large-batch routes.
Jordan: doing on-call handoff in 20m — @Maria can you own until then and escalate to infra if CPU stays high?
Maria: yep, will own. doing capacity shift and enabling fallback to smaller model-variant for heavy requests.
Kevin: quick monitoring note: we're getting heavy alert noise from the single-window rule. can we tune multi-window to avoid paging for short bursts?
Samira: propose multi-window strategy: require short-term window to be >8 (5m) AND medium-term (1h) >2 to page. that will catch sustained burns not transient spikes. also add budget threshold: only page if remaining_budget_pct < 70%.
Jordan: agree. we want page only when customer impact is meaningful and error budget is getting consumed. otherwise fire a non-paging alert to eng-monitoring channel.
Maria: draft of new Prometheus-like rule I'm testing:```
ALERT SLOBurnPaging
IF (burnrate_5m > 8 and burnrate_1h > 2 and slo_remaining_pct < 70)
FOR 2m
LABELS { severity = "page" }
```
Samira: also adding companion: non-paging noisy alert -> post to #eng-monitoring if 5m burnrate > 6 but budget > 70%.
Avery: we should also adjust paging criteria to check affected_customers_count > 2 or request_volume_pct > 1% so tiny tenants don't wake on-call.
Kevin: +1 to tenant threshold. otherwise we get waked for a single noisy customer.
Maria: created ticket INFRA-3421 to add the two rules and update alert docs, assigned to Samira. runbook updated to include new multi-window guidance.
Jordan: handoff: I'm passing on-call to Maria. leaving notes: current mitigations = throttle large batches, fallback to smaller model-variant, increased GC tuning on runtime. keep an eye on p99 and 429 rate.
Maria: noted. I'll keep monitoring for 30m then escalate if long-term burn doesn't drop.
Samira: follow-up items for postmortem / after-action:
- Add new dashboard panels: SLO burn rate (1m/5m/1h), remaining budget %, per-tenant impact count
- Add annotation in dashboard for when model-variant fallback triggers
- Create a suppression rule for synthetic/test traffic that was noisy in this incident
- Evaluate quantization profile that caused kv-cache behavior on xlarge-q4
Maria: I'll open the monitoring PR with the rule changes and dashboard JSON. tagging @Kevin for review.
Kevin: will review. Also recommend we add a non-paging grafana alert for 1m spikes so infra knows immediately but doesn't page.
Jordan: customer comms: no major outages, but some hosted customers saw increased latency and transient errors. @Avery can you queue a short status note for CS if this persists > 1h?
Avery: will prepare a draft.
Samira: final proposal for alert noise reduction:
- Multi-window gating: short + medium window
- Budget threshold gating: only page when budget < 70%
- Tenant volume gating: only page if affected tenants > 2 or req volume > 1%
- Non-paging channel for transients and a 1m spike alert to infra
Maria: implementing now. iterating quickly with small steps and monitoring to avoid masking real issues.
Jordan: thanks team. after-action: we should run a small tabletop next week to validate these rules with synthetic fires. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident REDWOOD-API resolved at 1718005600 (mitigations applied, SLO burn trending down).
